cost_basis: DERIVED, NOT MEASURED as a dollar figure -- this box cannot read its own billing (COMPUTE_BUDGET_CHARTER.md section 5, CLAUDE.md rule 12). The core-minute figure rests on a MEASURED, SUBOFF-SPECIFIC, CONTENDED rate, which is the whole point of this successor: R1's estimate rested on the single-tenant smoke_coarse rate and under-predicted by 2.68x, so R1's cap could not deliver R1's own registered endTime. THE NEW BASIS, from two independent contended points read from named log.simpleFoam files: reg_coarse 39,904 cells, 1,443 incremental iterations, 896 s wall -> 1.556056e-05 s per cell-iteration; reg_medium 89,784 cells, 309 incremental iterations, 433 s wall -> 1.560740e-05 s per cell-iteration. The two AGREE to 0.30% across a 2.25x change in cell count, so per-cell cost is FLAT at regression scale and extrapolation to the 202,014-cell fine level is measured-supported rather than assumed. The design rate D is the SLOWER of the two, 1.560740e-05 s/cell-iteration at ranks 1. At the INHERITED endTime 2500: coarse 39,904 x 2500 x D + 4 s setup = 1561.0 s = 26.02 core-min; medium 89,784 x 2500 x D + 8 s = 3511.2 s = 58.52 core-min; fine 202,014 x 2500 x D + 18 s [setup INFERRED by cell scaling, 0.2% of the level] = 7900.3 s = 131.67 core-min. TRIPLE = 216.2 core-min, which is what THIS entry spends. The registered sub-caps apply a margin M = 1.75 (a 1.60x bound on further bandwidth contention, since concurrent CPU-bound solvers cannot exceed nproc = 16 and were measured at 10, times 1.09 for the endTime field write, which is UNMEASURED because reg_coarse stopped at 1445 and never reached writeInterval 2500): 46 / 103 / 231 core-min -> wall timeouts 2760 / 6180 / 13860 s at ranks 1. Sum 380, plus 20 core-min of accounting reserve so the global guard cannot pre-empt a level its own sub-cap admits, = the registered cap 400 core-min. Every sub-cap reaches N ~ 4,400 against the registered 2,500, i.e. 1.76x margin; R1's coarse sub-cap reached 1,445 against 2,500, i.e. 0.58x, and that ratio is the defect being repaired. NO RERUN ALLOWANCE IS RESERVED: R1 reserved one and it bought nothing, and the honest answer to a stop is a re-registered successor, not a second helping. Dollars: 216.2/60 x $0.0513 = $0.1849 DERIVED for this entry, 400/60 x $0.0513 = $0.3420 DERIVED for the whole capped rung. CPU only, no GPU, so the 2026-08-21 blanket applies; far under the $25 pre-authorised tier. The cap is 2.67x R1's and costs 21 cents more -- which is why sizing a cap for thrift was never worth anything. _LAUNCH_GRADES_BY_DEFAULT: THIS IS THE SECOND DEFECT R1b REPAIRS AND IT IS WHY launch_cmd CARRIES NO FLAG. R1's launcher graded only under --grade and the R1 queue entry did not pass it, so with the fleet dead a clean R1 would have completed and produced NO VERDICT AT ALL. run_suboff_r1b_triple.sh HAS NO GRADE FLAG AT ALL -- not --grade, not --no-grade. It takes NO arguments; any argument but --help is refused (exit 2). Grading at the end of a clean triple is unconditional, and an EXIT trap (with TERM/INT/HUP routed into it) guarantees that verification/runs/navier_class/SUBOFF/VERDICT.R1b_triple.txt exists on EVERY termination path -- clean, refused, capped, crashed or killed. If that file is absent, the script never started. A non-grading run is therefore not expressible, and there is no flag for this entry to forget.
